Net income was $43.9 million and $36.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively, representing an increase of 19.7%. Diluted earnings per share (&#8220;EPS&#8221;) for the third quarter of 2026 were $1.59 compared to $1.16 for the second quarter of 2026. Diluted EPS was $4.17 and $3.45 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Earnings for the third quarter of 2026 reflected higher net interest income stemming from growth in all categories of average interest-earning assets, including growth in loans, as well as the recognition of a $920 thousand income tax benefit associated with the Bank's purchase of renewable energy tax credits at a discount during the third quarter. This income tax benefit increased both basic and diluted EPS by approximately $0.09 during the three and nine months ended September&#160;30, 2026. Earnings for the third quarter also benefited from the absence of $1.8 million of accelerated purchase discount accretion, which was recorded in the second quarter of 2026, and was associated with the redemption of higher-cost subordinated debentures assumed in the merger with 1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:6.82pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.67pt;vertical-align:baseline">st</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Capital Bancorp in 2024 (&#34;sub debt redemption&#34;). The sub debt redemption reduced both basic and diluted EPS by approximately $0.12 during the second quarter as well as for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. </font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#34;We delivered record quarterly earnings, marked by higher net interest income driven by solid loan growth </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8211; </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">particularly by our San Luis Obispo County team </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8211;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> and overall higher average interest-earning assets funded through healthy deposit growth during the quarter,&#8221; said Krista Snelling, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of West Coast Community Bancorp. &#34;This quarter saw tremendous momentum across the business, including our expansion into Silicon Valley and the Peninsula and our Nasdaq listing. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities and growth initiatives, such as hiring our Private Banking team and opening new branches.&#34;</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;text-align:justify"><font style="background-color:#fff7c3;color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"><br></font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">As previously announced on October 19, 2026, the Bancorp Board of Directors declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.29 per common share, reflecting a $0.04 per share increase over the previous quarterly dividend. This dividend is payable on or about November 6, 2026, to shareholders of record as of November 2, 2026. &#8220;Increasing the dividend reflects the strength of our business, the confidence of our Board in our capacity for future growth and a commitment to rewarding our shareholders,&#8221; added Snelling</font><font Please also see &#34;Non-GAAP Financial Measures&#34; below.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:18pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.33pt">Primary liquidity ratio, defined as cash and cash equivalents, deposits held in other banks and unpledged available for sale (&#8220;AFS&#8221;) securities as a percentage of total assets, was 11.7% and 13.0% at September&#160;30, 2026, and June&#160;30, 2026, respectively.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div id="ia33664b2a7254400a6c878436dfb6e22_159"></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline">Net Interest Income and Net Interest Margin</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Net interest income was $37.1 million for the third quarter of 2026, representing an increase of $4.0 million, or 12.0%, from $33.1 million for the second quarter of 2026. The quarter-over-quarter increase in net interest income is attributed to growth in average interest-earning assets during the third quarter and the absence of $1.8 million in accelerated accretion associated with the sub debt redemption that occurred in the second quarter. The increase in interest-earning assets is attributed to growth in loan balances during the quarter as well as higher average balances of investment securities and interest-earning cash. These increases were funded in part by higher average deposit balances during the quarter.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The taxable equivalent net interest margin, a non-GAAP measure, was 5.20% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 4.92% for the second quarter, or 5.19%, on an adjusted basis when excluding the impact of the sub debt redemption, a non-GAAP measure. The modest quarter-over-quarter increase in the adjusted taxable equivalent net interest margin can be attributed to slightly higher overall yields on average interest-earning assets, including a seven-basis-point increase in the average yield on loans during the third quarter. This was partially offset by a slight increase in the adjusted cost of funds, a non-GAAP measure, during the third quarter that can be attributed to growth in money market deposits, coupled with slightly higher overall rates on deposits during the third quarter. The cost of funds for the third quarter of 2026 was 1.31%, compared to 1.59% for the second quarter, or 1.29% on an adjusted basis when excluding the impact of the sub debt redemption in the second quarter, a non-GAAP measure. Please see &#34;Non-GAAP Financial Measures&#34; below.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:6.82pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.67pt;vertical-align:baseline">(1) Interest income on investment securities, interest income on loans, net interest income and net interest margin are presented here on a taxable equivalent basis, using the statutory federal income tax rate of 21 percent, and are non-GAAP financial measures. Please see &#34;Non-GAAP Financial Measures&#34; below.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:6.82pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.67pt;vertical-align:baseline">(2) Average balances on loans outstanding include nonaccrual loans, unamortized net deferred loan fees&#47;costs and unaccreted purchase discount on acquired loans. The amortization of net loan origination fees and accretion of purchase discount on acquired loans are included in interest income on loans.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div id="ia33664b2a7254400a6c878436dfb6e22_166"></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline">Noninterest Income </font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Noninterest income for the third quarter of 2026 was $1.3 million, compared to $1.2 million for the second quarter of 2026. The quarter-over-quarter increase is largely attributed to a $153 thousand special dividend that was received on our holdings of FHLB of San Francisco stock during the third quarter.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline">Noninterest Expense </font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Noninterest expense for the third quarter of 2026 was $16.3 million, compared to $15.9 million for the second quarter of 2026. The quarter-over-quarter increase is largely attributed to increases in data and item processing costs, professional fees and various other miscellaneous expenses, partially offset by a decrease in salaries and employee benefits. The increase in data and item processing costs during the third quarter is primarily associated with the absence of one-time credits received from our core system processor that were utilized in the second quarter. The increase in professional fees can be attributed to expenses incurred related to Bancorp becoming an SEC registrant and a Nasdaq-listed company in the third quarter, as well as various other expenses associated with regular third-party credit reviews and other consulting fees. The decline in salaries and employee benefits during the quarter was primarily associated with the absence of expense associated with annual director stock grants that occurred in the second </font></div><div style="height:45pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">6</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:45pt;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">quarter, as well as increased compensation deferrals attributed to successful loan originations during the third quarter.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div id="ia33664b2a7254400a6c878436dfb6e22_182"></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline">Investment Portfolio</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Securities issued by U.S. government-sponsored agencies, U.S. Treasury bonds and Small Business Administration (&#34;SBA&#34;) securities accounted for 52%, 26% and 1%, respectively, of the investment portfolio as of September&#160;30, 2026. These securities carry explicit or implicit credit guarantees from the U.S. government and thus present minimal credit or liquidity risk. Municipal bonds, corporate bonds and private-label collateralized mortgage obligations&#47;asset-backed instruments represent 17%, 2% and 2% of the carrying value of the portfolio, respectively, as of September&#160;30, 2026.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The investment portfolio totaled $377.9 million at September&#160;30, 2026, compared to $388.1 million at June&#160;30, 2026. The decrease in the investment portfolio from June&#160;30, 2026, was primarily due to an increase in unrealized losses on AFS securities of $14.8 million, stemming from a rise in intermediate-term interest rates during the period, and maturities, paydowns and sales during the third quarter totaling $16.0&#160;million, partially offset by purchases of U.S. Treasury securities, totaling $19.9 million. The investment portfolio had an effective duration of 3.8 years as of September&#160;30, 2026, and June&#160;30, 2026. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Net unrealized losses on AFS securities were $23.8 million, or $16.8 million after-tax, at September&#160;30, 2026, compared to $9.0 million, or $6.3 million after-tax, at June&#160;30, 2026.</font></div><div id="ia33664b2a7254400a6c878436dfb6e22_192"></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline">Loans and Asset Quality</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Total loans, net of unaccreted purchase discount and deferred fees and costs, increased $65.6 million, or 2.9%, from June&#160;30, 2026. Loan growth during the third quarter of 2026 was largely attributed to increases in revolving commercial lines, which grew by $66.4 million during the quarter. This increase was primarily attributed to agriculture-related lending by the Bank's San Luis Obispo County team. New loan commitments originated during the third quarter were $199.1 million, driven by $86.8 million in new commercial and industrial (&#8220;C&#38;I&#8221;) commitments and $57.9 million in new commercial real estate (&#8220;CRE&#8221;) loan commitments.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Nonaccrual loans of $11.9 million accounted for 0.51% of total loans at September&#160;30, 2026, compared to $11.4 million, or 0.50%, of total loans at June&#160;30, 2026. At September&#160;30, 2026, nonaccrual loans included a $5.8 million hotel relationship, consisting of two loans, of which one has an SBA guarantee of approximately $3.7 million. Other nonaccrual loans at September&#160;30, 2026, consisted primarily of SBA-related credits totaling $4.7 million that contained SBA guarantees of approximately $4.0 million, and two CRE loans totaling approximately $1.4 million. At September&#160;30, 2026, government guarantees of $7.8 million reduced net credit exposure on nonaccrual loans to approximately $4.1 million.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Accruing loans past due 30-89 days totaled $2.3</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> million</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> at September&#160;30, 2026, an increase from $1.2 million at June&#160;30, 2026. The balance of accruing loans past due 30-89 days primarily reflects a $1.9 million substandard CRE loan that is secured by a mixed-use property. There were no loans more than 90 days past due still accruing as of September&#160;30, 2026, or June&#160;30, 2026.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The ACL on loans was $36.6 million at September&#160;30, 2026, or 1.57%, of total loans, compared to $35.1 million at June&#160;30, 2026, or 1.55%, of total loans. The increase in the ACL during the third quarter is attributed to several factors including organic loan growth and changes in portfolio mix which increased the ACL by approximately $1.5 million, and a $1.2 million increase in the ACL for certain individually evaluated loans. These increases were partially offset by lower pooled reserve rates reflecting improvements in the economic forecast as well as improvements in certain qualitative factors used in the ACL model. The provision for credit losses on loans was $275 thousand for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $1.4 million in the second quarter of 2026. The quarter-over-quarter decrease in the provision is largely attributed to the factors just discussed in addition to the full recovery, upon payoff, of a previously substantially charged-off loan in the amount of $1.2 million that occurred in the third quarter.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="height:45pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">7</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:45pt;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Bank recorded net recoveries for the third quarter of 2026 of $1.2 million. Net recoveries for the quarter were largely attributed to the full recovery previously discussed.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:115%">The ACL for unfunded commitments, recorded in other liabilities, was $2.6 million, or 0.38% of unfunded credit commitments at September&#160;30, 2026, compared to $2.9 million, or 0.42%, at June&#160;30, 2026. The decrease in the ACL for unfunded commitments reflected, in part, higher utilization of commercial lines, which reduced unfunded commitments, and lower reserve rates consistent with improvements in the qualitative factors used to determine the ACL for funded loans. Total unfunded commitments decreased by approximately $6.3 million during the third quarter to $675.0 million as of September&#160;30, 2026. </font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div id="ia33664b2a7254400a6c878436dfb6e22_244"></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;text-align:justify"><font September&#160;30, 2026, a $4.1 million, or 1.0%, increase compared to June&#160;30, 2026. Tangible common equity, a non-GAAP measure, was $341.6 million at September&#160;30, 2026, a $5.1 million, or 1.5%, increase compared to June&#160;30, 2026. The quarter-over-quarter change in tangible common equity is largely attributed to net income of $16.7 million, activity related to stock-based compensation and the amortization of core deposit intangibles, together totaling $1.5 million, partially offset by an increase in accumulated other comprehensive loss of $10.5 million due to higher unrealized losses on AFS investment securities during the quarter, and dividends declared of </font></div><div style="height:45pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">9</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:45pt;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">$2.6 million. Tangible book value per share, a non-GAAP measure, was $32.46 at September&#160;30, 2026, compared to $32.01 at June&#160;30, 2026. Please see &#34;Non-GAAP Financial Measures&#34; below.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div id="ia33664b2a7254400a6c878436dfb6e22_224"></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline">ABOUT WEST COAST COMMUNITY BANCORP AND WEST COAST COMMUNITY BANK</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">West Coast Community Bancorp is the bank holding company for West Coast Community Bank. Founded in 2004, the Bank is a top-rated, locally operated and full-service community bank headquartered in Santa Cruz, Calif. with branches in Aptos, Capitola, King City, Monterey, Salinas, San Jose, San Luis Obispo, San Mateo, Santa Cruz, Scotts Valley and Watsonville. West Coast Community Bank is distinguished from &#34;big banks&#34; by its relationship-based service, problem-solving focus and direct access to decision makers. The Bank also is an SBA Preferred Lending Partner. As a full-service bank, West Coast Community Bank offers competitive deposit and lending solutions for businesses and individuals&#59; including business loans, lines of credit, commercial real estate financing, construction lending, asset-based lending, agricultural loans, SBA and USDA government guaranteed loans, credit cards, merchant services, remote deposit capture, mobile and online banking, bill payment and treasury management. Additional information regarding the Company&#8217;s recent industry recognition, community engagement, and financial performance is included in the accompanying investor presentation and at investors.wccb.com.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div id="ia33664b2a7254400a6c878436dfb6e22_232"></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Forward-Looking Statements</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">This release may contain statements that we believe are, or may be considered to be, &#8220;forward-looking statements&#8221; within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline">Non-GAAP Financial Measures</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%"> </font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In addition to presenting the Company&#8217;s results of operations in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;) in the United States of America, certain financial measures discussed herein are non-GAAP financial measures, examples of which include taxable equivalent net interest income, efficiency ratio, tangible common equity ratio and return on average tangible equity. Generally, a non-GAAP measure is a numerical measure of a company&#8217;s financial performance, financial position or cash flows that exclude (or include) amounts that are included in (or excluded from) the most directly comparable measure calculated and presented in accordance with GAAP. We believe that the non-GAAP financial measures used herein provide helpful additional information about our operating results, performance trends and financial condition. Non-GAAP measures should not be considered a substitute for GAAP results and may not be comparable to similar measures used by other banking companies, among other limitations. Other companies may use the same or similar names for non-GAAP measures but may calculate them differently. As a result, caution should be used when comparing the Company's non-GAAP measures with those of other companies.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Investors are encouraged to review the reconciliation of non-GAAP financial measures used herein to their most directly comparable GAAP financial measures, which are presented in the tables below.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="height:45pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">13</font></div></div></div><div id="ia33664b2a7254400a6c878436dfb6e22_16"></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:45pt;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The following tables present non-GAAP financial measures management believes provide useful information for understanding the operating results of our core business and a better comparison of financial performance.
